preconditions.description: The number of stations n is between 3 and 3000 inclusive.
Each of the n lines after the first contains exactly two integers.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n and 1 <= int(y) <= n for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x, y in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: Each station number in the passages is between 1 and n inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(int(x) != int(y) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x, y in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: No passage connects a station to itself.

preconditions.expression: len({(int(x), int(y)) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x, y in [line.split()]}) == n
preconditions.description: There are exactly n passages, each connecting a unique pair of stations.

preconditions.expression: len({(int(x), int(y)) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x, y in [line.split()]}) + len({(int(y), int(x)) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x, y in [line.split()]}) == 2 * n
preconditions.description: The graph is undirected (each passage is counted once in each direction).

preconditions.expression: len({int(x) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x, y in [line.split()]}) == n and len({int(y) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x, y in [line.split()]}) == n
preconditions.description: All stations are connected by at least one passage.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n space-separated integers.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(d) for d in stdout.split())
postconditions.description: Each distance is a non-negative integer.

postconditions.expression: all(int(d) == 0 for d in stdout.split() if int(x) in ringroad and int(y) in ringroad for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x, y in [line.split()] if int(x) == int(y))
postconditions.description: Stations on the ringroad have distance 0.

postconditions.expression: all(int(d) == min(steps for steps in [BFS_distance(int(x), ringroad) for x in range(1, n+1)]) for d in stdout.split())
postconditions.description: The distance of each station is the minimum number of passages required to reach any station on the ringroad.

invariants.expression: len(ringroad) == n and all(ringroad[i] != ringroad[(i+1)%len(ringroad)] for i in range(len(ringroad))) and all((ringroad[i], ringroad[(i+1)%len(ringroad)]) in edges or (ringroad[(i+1)%len(ringroad)], ringroad[i]) in edges for i in range(len(ringroad)))
invariants.description: The ringroad is a cycle of all stations in the graph, where each consecutive pair is connected by a passage.

invariants.expression: len(ringroad) == n and all(ringroad[i] != ringroad[j] for i in range(len(ringroad)) for j in range(i+1, len(ringroad)))
invariants.description: The ringroad contains each station exactly once.
